topics.title: Node.js Architecture
topics.content:
### Single-Threaded, Non-Blocking I/O

Node.js runs on a **single thread** but handles thousands of concurrent connections through its **event loop** and **non-blocking I/O**.

```
                       ┌─────────────────────┐
  Incoming requests →  │    Event Loop        │
                       │  (Single Thread)     │
                       └──────────┬──────────┘
                                  │
              ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
              ▼                   ▼                   ▼
        File System          Database I/O        Network I/O
        (libuv pool)        (async driver)      (async socket)
              │                   │                   │
              └───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
                                  │
                             Callbacks fire
                          back on event loop
```

The key insight: Node doesn't wait for I/O. It registers a callback and moves on to handle other requests.

```js
// Blocking (bad in Node — freezes entire server)
const data = fs.readFileSync('/large-file.csv'); // All other requests wait

// Non-blocking (correct)
fs.readFile('/large-file.csv', (err, data) => {
  // Fires when file is ready; other requests handled in the meantime
});

// Modern async/await (same non-blocking, cleaner syntax)
const data = await fs.promises.readFile('/large-file.csv');
```
